title: Why the S&P at Record Highs Is Hiding a Broken Market
speaker: Jim Welsh (Macro Tides), interviewed by Ilya Spivak

macro_themes.view: S&P new highs are driven by semis and Mag 7; equal-weight relative strength is the lowest in 24 years and the A/D line is below mid-August.

macro_themes.theme: Treasury yields drive the broad market
macro_themes.view: Broad market is hostage to rising yields; only a 30-40bp decline over 1-3 months would bring broad participation.
No hike in October, December hike likely; Fed under Warsh is credibly hawkish; next year depends on data, especially oil.
A 1987-style 22% rise in the 10-year would take it to ~5.65%, a potential breaking point.
Stocks overvalued, household equity exposure at record; expects a secular bear market (years out) with ~50% declines; semis could lose ~65% as in 2001-02/2008.
Republicans likely lose the House; market has anticipated it, knee-jerk reaction only.

calls.condition: S&P can reach 8000 only if Treasury yields fall 30-40bp and the broad market joins; if yields keep rising tech cracks
calls.reason: Narrow leadership; yields are the swing factor; secular bear market expected over coming years.
calls.quote: that's how the S&P can get to 8,000 because you're going to need that participation from the broad market
